blocks.text: Quick verdict

Bright Data is the most complete enterprise replacement for NetNut: a 150M+ residential pool, ISP, datacenter and mobile networks, ZIP, ASN and carrier targeting, and managed Web Unlocker, SERP API and Scraping Browser products, backed by KYC and compliance processes that procurement teams can review. It costs more at entry ($8/GB list, often discounted 50%), but monthly plans fall to $2.50/GB, close to NetNut's old volume rates. For large ad-verification and scraping operations, it is the lowest-risk landing spot.

Bright Data and NetNut were two of the best-known enterprise residential networks, and NetNut often pitched itself as a faster, ISP-sourced alternative to Bright Data. That rivalry ended on July 2, 2026, when the FBI seized NetNut's domains after Google linked its residential pool to the Popa botnet. For enterprise teams, Bright Data is now one of the most obvious places to move. This page compares what NetNut offered with Bright Data's current platform and explains how to migrate.
What happened to NetNut?

NetNut stopped being a normal buying option on July 2, 2026. That day the FBI and IRS Criminal Investigation seized NetNut-related domains, and Google published research linking the network's residential exit nodes to the Popa botnet, which it estimated at two million or more hijacked home devices. NetNut's parent, Alarum Technologies, rejects the allegations, but its main domains went on to show seizure banners and its share price fell sharply. Whatever the final legal outcome, routing business traffic through that infrastructure now carries legal and reputational risk.

blocks.text: Bright Data in 2026: what you get

Bright Data is the largest and most complete web-data platform in this market. Beyond residential proxies it sells datacenter, ISP and mobile networks, an unblocking API, a SERP API, a hosted Scraping Browser and ready-made datasets, each billed on its own meter. Its residential network is advertised at more than 150 million IPs in 195 countries, with targeting down to ZIP code and ASN. The trade-off is cost and complexity: the list price sits at the top of the market and the dashboard is built around zones, rules and compliance checks rather than a two-click setup.

Bright Data, formerly Luminati, is the default enterprise pick for teams that want every collection tool under one contract. Its residential pool is one of the deepest available (150M+ advertised IPs across 195 countries), targeting goes down to city, ZIP and ASN, and the company layers managed products such as Web Unlocker and the Scraping Browser on top. You pay for that breadth: entry pricing is the highest of the major providers unless a promotion is running, and access to some target categories requires a compliance review.

Strengths: Deepest targeting in the market (ZIP, ASN, carrier); Managed unblocking, SERP and browser products under one account; Mature compliance and KYC processes that enterprise buyers ask for; Very large residential pool for high-rotation work. Weak spots: Highest list price per GB at low volume; Dashboard and zone setup take time to learn; Some targets need a compliance review before access.
What NetNut offered, and how Bright Data compares

Before the seizure, NetNut was best known for ISP-sourced static residential proxies and a fast rotating residential network aimed at scraping, ad verification and brand-protection teams. Its residential rates generally ran from about $1.87 to $3.53 per GB on larger plans, with higher effective prices on entry plans. Bright Data covers much of the same ground: datacenter, isp, mobile, web unlocker, serp api, scraping browser, datasets sit alongside its residential network, which advertises 150M+ IPs in 195 countries.
What former NetNut customers need, and whether Bright Data
delivers

Most NetNut accounts were built around three things: static ISP IPs for long-lived sessions, rotating residential traffic with US state and city targeting, and high concurrency for scraping. On static ISP-style IPs, Bright Data's answer is yes; its other products are datacenter, ISP, mobile, Web Unlocker, SERP API, Scraping Browser, datasets. On rotating residential targeting, Bright Data offers country, state, city, ZIP, ASN and carrier in 195 countries, with rotating per request or sticky sessions you control per zone. On billing, Bright Data uses pay-as-you-go or monthly plans with included GB, and unused traffic is handled as follows: monthly plan allowances reset each cycle. Map each of your old NetNut zones to one of these before you migrate, so nothing breaks on the day you switch.
Bright Data pricing

Bright Data lists residential traffic at $8/GB pay-as-you-go with no commitment, and it frequently runs 50%-off promotions that bring that to about $4/GB. Monthly plans start with the Growth tier at $499 for roughly 141 GB (about $3.50/GB) and fall to around $2.50/GB on the largest public plan.

Quick cost check for Bright Data: 10 GB comes to $80 PAYG list (about $40 when the half-price promo runs), and 100 GB comes to $499 Growth plan (141 GB included, about $3.50/GB). NetNut's larger plans used to run about $1.87-$3.53/GB, so compare against what you actually paid rather than NetNut's headline rate.
How to migrate from NetNut to Bright Data
1. Export your NetNut usage history and list the countries, cities and session types you actually used, so you can map them to Bright Data's targeting (country, state, city, ZIP, ASN and carrier).
2. Test before you commit. Bright Data's testing option: free trial for business accounts, no card required. Run your real targets for a day on the smallest purchase before moving production traffic.
3. Swap the gateway host and credentials in your scraper or browser profiles. Bright Data supports HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS5.
4. Compare success rate, response time and cost per successful request against your old NetNut baseline, then move traffic over in stages.
5. Remove any NetNut SDKs, browser extensions or endpoints from your systems, and rotate any credentials that were stored alongside them.
Where Bright Data fits best
General web scraping: strong fit. Why: its pool depth and Web Unlocker handle hardened targets.
SERP and rank tracking: strong fit. Why: it sells a dedicated SERP API alongside raw proxies.
Social media and multi-account management: workable. Why: it is powerful but expensive for low-volume account work.
E-commerce price and stock monitoring: strong fit. Why: ZIP-level targeting suits local pricing and stock checks.
Ad verification and geo-testing: strong fit. Why: carrier and ASN targeting reproduce what real users see.
Tight budgets: weak fit. Why: its list price is the highest in this comparison.
Protocols and sessions

Bright Data supports HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS5 and offers rotating per request or sticky sessions you control per zone. Targeting covers country, state, city, ZIP, ASN and carrier across 195 countries. Like NetNut's residential gateway, it works through a single backconnect endpoint with location and session options passed in the username, plus IP whitelisting.
How to vet a residential proxy provider after NetNut

The NetNut case showed that a residential pool can look like a normal enterprise product while resting on devices whose owners never meaningfully agreed to share their connection. Before you move traffic to any provider, including Bright Data, ask a few direct questions and keep the answers on file:
How are residential IPs sourced? Look for an opt-in SDK or app programme with clear user
consent and compensation, and ask which partner apps are involved.
Does the provider publish an ethics or sourcing policy, and has it been audited or certified (for
example AppEsteem or ISO 27001)?
What KYC does the provider apply to customers, and which target categories are restricted?
Strict onboarding is a good sign, not an inconvenience.
How does it handle abuse reports, and is there a named legal entity and jurisdiction behind the
service?
Can you get contractual assurances, such as a data-processing agreement, if your compliance
team needs them?
Bottom line

NetNut is no longer a provider you can plan around, so the real decision is which network replaces it. Bright Data is strongest for enterprise data teams with budget for managed tooling and hard targets where unblocking APIs save engineering time, starts at $8/GB pay-as-you-go list price (50%-off promos are frequent), and offers free trial for business accounts, no card required. Test it on your own targets for a day, compare cost per successful request with your old NetNut baseline, and move production traffic in stages.
